subject: Error in create.bins(data, cutpoints) with NA (transects with no detection)

messages.author: 81e473ecfda78ff0
messages.subject: Error in create.bins(data, cutpoints) with NA (transects with no detection)
parts:
Dear List,

 

I am running analysis using Distance in R, but I get the following error message when I try to fit a distance function ds()

 

Error in create.bins(data, cutpoints) :

Some distances are NA, can't create bins.

 

We conducted an aerial survey of seals. Perpendicular distance was recorded in 5 bins, with the first bin left truncated by 35m because observers could not view the line directly below the aircraft. In total, 31 transects were flown, but seals were only sighted on 29 of these.

For transects on which no sightings were made there needs to be a record for the transect (so that field effort is accurately recorded) but the perpendicular distance is set to "NA" (it takes on no value) (I import these as a blank cells in a .csv file).

 

However, it seems that these are causing me some difficulty (the code runs if I exclude transects without any observations). Any guidance will be much appreciated!

 

Some further details:

Using ‘Distance’ version 0.9.4 in R version 3.2.2.

 

dist.bins <- c(35.2,51.16,72.66, 105.6, 167.5,345.73)

 

df <- ds(distdata , transect="line", key="hr", adjustment="poly",

                              truncation=list(left=35.2,right=345.73), cutpoints=dist.bins,                       

                              convert.units = 0.001)

 

With thanks,

Chris

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error in create.bins(data, cutpoints) with NA (transects with no detection)
parts:
Chris

There are 'empty' transects (transects without sightings) in the minke example data set, that I used for the example I just sent along to John Edwards.  As you will see if you run the example code from my last posting upon the minke data,  no errors are generated.

You will note from the example code that I created the sequence of cutpoints using max(); i.e. no truncation and furthermore, when using max() to build the sequence, I invoked the na.rm=TRUE option so that max() would not complain about the NAs in the dataset.  I had a brief glance at the 'create.bins()' code, and saw that NAs were explicitly dealt with, but came to no other conclusions.

I don't have an answer as to why, with our datasets being similar with regard to NAs, my 'minke' example works and yours does not.  Perhaps more clever minds will intercede.
